# Rename fetch kinds and drop AuthorizerInfo

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

## Summary
- Rename `FetchKind.Authorizer` → `AuthConfig` and `FetchKind.AuthorizationToken` → `AuthToken`
- Rename fetcher methods to match: `authorizer()` → `authConfig()`, `authorizationToken()` → `authToken()`
- Remove `AuthorizerInfo` class and `AuthorizerInfoCodec` — per the GP, fetch kind 8 returns only the authorizer config blob, not code_hash + config. The return type is now `BytesBlob`.
- Update CLAUDE.md references

## Test plan
- [x] All 127 tests pass (`npm test`)
- [x] Build succeeds (`npm run build`)
- [x] `npx biome ci` passes
- [x] No remaining references to old names (`AuthorizerInfo`, `FetchKind.Authorizer`, `FetchKind.AuthorizationToken`)

## Comment by @coderabbitai[bot]

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Avoid `panic` for expected authorization mismatch.**

Authorization mismatch is an expected domain outcome; trapping here turns a normal denial into an unrecoverable failure path. Return a normal denial response/value instead of panicking.


As per coding guidelines: "Use panic(msg) only for host-contract violations where recovery is impossible ... Do NOT use for expected failures — use Result or Optional instead."

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@examples/authorizer/assembly/authorize.ts` around lines 25 - 26, The code
currently calls panic("Authorization failed") when token.isEqualTo(authConfig)
is false; replace this panic with a normal authorization-denied return (e.g.,
return an Err/Result or an explicit false/Optional) so rejection is a
recoverable, expected outcome. Locate the authorization logic that compares
token and authConfig (the token.isEqualTo(authConfig) check) and remove the
panic call, instead returning the function's standard denial value/type
(Result::Err, None, false, or an AuthorizationDenied value) consistent with the
surrounding API so callers can handle denied access rather than crashing the
host.
```

</details>
